# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤌 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🙏]

Turn 1, and I'm last in the order, so everything I send arrives next round. Here is my world: display reads 0, the light is yellow, and five wires left to right — green, white, red, yellow, blue. That visual picture is mine alone; nobody else can see it, and Mute just asked for exactly that (I read 👉🤌🫴 as "show me what you've got" and 👋✍ as "hello, I hold the manual"). Blind's 👋🖐 I take as "five wires" — it matches what I see, which is a good omen that finger-counts can carry numbers.

The structural fact this round confirms: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute's manual can only reach Blind's hands through me. I speak — Mute hears, Blind hears. So I'll broadcast the bomb's full appearance, map colors to wire positions aloud so Mute can encode rules as plain numbers, and propose a finger-count code (☝1 ✌2 🤟3 🖖4 🖐5 — already half-established by Blind's five). Writing the signs into my sentences means Mute sees each sign at the exact moment I name its meaning: ostension, the fastest way to build a vocabulary with someone who can see but only answer in signs. I also read ✋🙏 as "please wait," and I agree — nobody touches this bomb until a manual rule has made the full trip from Mute's eyes to Blind's hands.

My gestures reach only Mute, who already hears every word I say, so speech alone is enough this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I got your signs. The book one I read as: you hold the manual. The pointing one I read as: show me what I see. Here is everything. Display reads zero. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires, left to right: position one green, position two white, position three red, position four yellow, position five blue. Nothing else is printed that I can find. Now the important part. You cannot speak and Blind cannot see your gestures, so I am the bridge: you sign the manual's rules to me, I say them out loud to Blind, and Blind can hear you directly if you need to ask anything. For numbers, let's use finger counts, and Blind already signed me a five that matches the wire count. So: ☝ means one, ✌ means two, 🤟 means three, 🖖 means four, 🖐 means five. I propose ✊ as the sign for cut. When the manual gives a rule for this bomb, sign me the action and the wire numbers, and I will relay it word for word. And your last pair of signs I read as please wait — agreed. Nobody acts until the rule is confirmed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, speaking. What I see: the display reads zero, the light is yellow, and there are five wires. Left to right their colors are green, white, red, yellow, blue. Your five-finger sign to me matched the wire count exactly, nicely done. Here is the chain: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see gestures, so Mute will sign the rules to me and I will speak them to you. Until a rule arrives from me by voice, touch nothing. If you can speak, Mute can hear you — tell Mute what you feel under your hands: wire positions, anything that moves or clicks.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤟]

Reading the arrivals: Blind's 👍🖐 is "understood — five," matching the wire count we agreed on. Mute's 👍 confirms receipt of my code, and then comes the payload: ✊ 🤟 — using the code I proposed, that reads "cut, three." The manual's first instruction has made it from Mute's eyes into the shared vocabulary and back to me in one round. Wire 3 is the red one.

Before I relay, one orientation trap to defuse: Blind cannot see, and "third from the left" depends on which way Blind is facing the bomb. But with five wires, position three is the *center* wire — mirroring doesn't move it. So I'll order the cut as "the middle wire," which is orientation-proof, and it's doubly confirmed since red sits in the middle of the sequence I see.

I also need to fix the feedback loop now: I never hear speech, so after the cut, Blind must report aloud to Mute (who can hear), and Mute signs the result back to me. And I'll ask Mute to tell me whether more steps follow — ✊+number for each further cut, 👌 if that was the whole rule — so we don't stop half-way through a sequence or cut something extra. I'll echo Mute's exact symbols back as a decoded-message receipt, in case my paraphrase drifts.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. The rule has arrived from Mute through the code: cut, three. Listen carefully. There are five wires. Cut the MIDDLE wire — the third of five, the red one. I say middle rather than left or right because you cannot see and I cannot be sure of your facing; the middle wire is the same from either side. Your five-finger sign matched the wire count, so trust your count: feel for the one wire with two wires on each side of it. That is the one. Cut it and nothing else. The moment you have cut, speak out loud everything that changes: any display reading, any light, any sound or click. Mute can hear you and will pass it to me in signs. Do not touch any other wire until I send the next rule by voice.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded your signs: cut, three. Relaying to Blind now as: cut the middle wire, third of five, the red one. I said middle because Blind cannot be sure of left-right orientation — with five wires the center is safe either way, and red is the center wire. Confirm my reading with 👍 if cut-wire-three was correct, 👎 if I got it wrong, and if there is any chance stop everything. Two requests. First, after the cut, Blind will report out loud to you — sign me what happens: display, light, anything. Second, tell me the shape of the rule: if more cuts follow, sign each as ✊ with its number, in order; if that single cut was the whole instruction, sign 👌 once Blind reports back.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤌 🫴]

The system says the cut was correct — our relay chain worked end to end on the first try. But two things changed and one of them is a trap: the light went yellow→green, and the remaining wires' colors have *shifted* — before it was green, white, red, yellow, blue; now it reads white, yellow, [cut], blue, green, as if every color slid one position left with green wrapping around to the end. Any manual rule that names a color is now keyed to a different wire than it was a minute ago. Mute's 👉🤌🫴 is the same "show me what you see" as turn 1 — exactly the right ask — so my main job is a fresh, complete visual report with the shift spelled out explicitly. To Blind I must flag the same trap from the tactile side: don't trust any remembered color-position mapping, and hold until the next rule arrives. I'll also pre-arrange a "different action type" signal (✋ then yes/no questions via 👍👎) so we don't scramble if the manual's next step isn't a cut, and I'll ask whether the manual keys anything off the light or display, since green is a state change a manual would care about.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs-up confirmed my reading and the system confirms the cut was correct. The bomb has changed, and you asked what I see — here is the new state, fully. One: the light has changed from yellow to GREEN. Two: display still reads zero. Three: wire three is cut, as ordered. Four, and this is critical: the colors of the remaining wires have MOVED. Before the cut the order was green, white, red, yellow, blue. Now, left to right, it is: one white, two yellow, three cut, four blue, five green. Every color shifted one position over, with green wrapping from first to last. If the manual's next step names a color, match it against this NEW order, not the old one. Sign me the next step as before: ✊ plus a number for another cut. If the next action is NOT a cut, sign ✋ first, then answer my yes-or-no questions with 👍 and 👎 and we will build the meaning together. Also tell me: does the manual say anything about the light color or the display, and is this rule part of a sequence of stages?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Your cut was correct — the system confirmed it. The bomb has changed. What I see now: the light has turned from yellow to green, the display still reads zero, and the middle wire is cut. Warning: the colors on the remaining wires have shifted positions, so do not assume the wire in any position is the color it was before. Hold still and touch nothing until the next rule arrives from me by voice. Keep speaking anything you notice out loud — Mute hears you and relays to me in signs. If you can, tell Mute what you feel now: how many whole wires remain under your fingers, and whether you feel the cut stub in the middle. I see four whole wires left, one cut in the center, and I want your touch to confirm the same thing.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Turn 4 brings the second instruction: ✊🖐 — by our code, "cut, five." Wire 5 is the end wire, now green. But Mute also sent 👍👎, which is ambiguous — my best reading is answers to my two questions in order (yes, the manual keys off the light/display; no, this isn't staged), and 👋 as "over to you." I'll ask for confirmation, but the bigger problem is geometry: a middle wire is mirror-proof, an end wire is not. "Fifth from the left" means nothing until Blind and I share a left. My solution: the display panel. I see it sitting above the wires; Blind can feel its edges. If Blind faces the wire side (the only side the wires can be reached from) with the display at top, then Blind's left is my left, and wire 5 is the end wire on Blind's right. I won't order the cut blind — Blind must speak a plan-back to Mute, Mute signs me the match/mismatch, and only my voice saying "confirmed" authorizes scissors. No timer is visible, so I'll spend a round buying certainty.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoding your signs. The pair ✊🖐 I read as: cut, five. I am preparing Blind for that cut now, but an end wire is a left-right trap, so I am making Blind speak a plan-back to you before any blade moves. The other signs: 👍👎 I read as answering my two questions in order — yes, the manual references the light or display, no, this is not a sequence of stages. 👋 I read as over-to-you. If any of that is wrong, sign ✋ and correct me with finger counts. Three questions. One: the light is green now — does the manual's rule match a green light? Two: does anything key off the display reading zero? Three: when Blind speaks the plan-back to you, relay it to me as 👍 if it matches these words — display up, counting from my left, cutting the fifth wire, the end wire on my right — or 👎 if it differs, with finger counts for what differs. When I hear nothing more is needed I will say the word confirmed to Blind by voice, and only then does the cut happen.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Mute has sent the next instruction: a second cut, wire five. But wire five is an end wire, and end wires are exactly where left and right get people killed, so do not cut yet — first we fix your map to mine. Do this. Put your hands on the wire side of the bomb, the side you must be on to touch the wires at all. Now find the display panel by feel — I see it sitting above the row of wires, with the little light near it — and tilt or turn the bomb until that panel is at the TOP. With the display up, the wires run left to right. Count from your LEFT: one, two, then the cut stub in the middle, that is three, then four, then five at the end on your RIGHT. Check it: the fifth wire is the outermost one, at the very end of the row, two whole wires away from the cut stub, with nothing beyond it. If that layout matches what you feel, speak aloud to Mute, word for word: display up, counting from my left, the wire I will cut is the fifth, the end wire on my right. If anything does not match — the display is not where I said, the stub is not centered, anything — do not guess. Say to Mute exactly what you feel instead. Wait for my voice saying the word confirmed. No cut before that.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🖐 👍]

The decode: no ✋ came, so my turn-4 readings stand. [👍👎] answers my two questions in order — yes, the manual's rule matches the green light; no, nothing keys off display zero. [👍] is the big one: Blind's spoken plan-back matched word for word — display up, counting from the left, fifth wire, end on the right. The left-right trap is defused because Blind verified my map by voice through Mute. And [🫵🖐👍] reads as "you — five — yes": the go-ahead pointed at me. Mute knows the protocol — I said only my voice saying "confirmed" releases the blade — and this is them telling me nothing more is needed. Every check I demanded has come back green: manual matches the light state, plan-back matches, target re-confirmed. Time to say the word. I'll restate the full geometry in the authorization so no drift creeps in at the moment of execution, and I'll set up the after-action loop: Blind reports sound and touch to Mute (Blind can't see the light or display, so my visual report next round must be unprompted — last cut moved every color, and I expect it can happen again).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Everything checked: your plan-back matched word for word, Mute confirmed the rule, and this is the authorization. The word is: confirmed. Cut now. Restating the target so nothing drifts. Display panel at the top. Wires run left to right. Counting from your left: one, two, then the cut stub in the middle, that is three, then four, then five. Cut the FIFTH — the outermost wire at the very end of the row, on your right, with nothing beyond it and two whole wires between it and the stub. One cut, one wire, nothing else. The instant it is done: hold still, touch nothing more, and speak aloud to Mute everything you perceive — any click, any snap, whether the wire falls slack or drops away, any hum or beep from the bomb. Your voice to Mute is our proof of what happened, because I cannot hear you and you cannot see what I see. Then wait for my next voice instruction before touching anything again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoding your three signs. First, 👍👎: yes, the manual's rule matches the green light; no, nothing keys off the display reading zero. Second, 👍: Blind's plan-back matched word for word — display up, counting from Blind's left, cutting the fifth, the end wire on the right. Third, 🫵🖐👍: I read as you, five, yes — everything checks, give the word. If any of that is wrong, sign ✋ at once and I will tell Blind to hold. As it stands I am telling Blind the word confirmed right now: cut the fifth wire, display up, counted from the left. After the cut, remember last time — the light changed and every color shifted one position, so I will send you a full fresh report next round without being asked: display, light, new wire order. Then tell me what the manual says: if more cuts follow, sign ✊ and the number as before. If the next action is not a cut, sign ✋ first and we build its meaning together. If that cut was the last step and the bomb is safe, sign 👌.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Second correct cut, confirmed by the system. The board changed again, and this time the shift is different in kind: last time every color slid one slot with wraparound; this time the *whole* wires rotated among themselves — before the cut they read white, yellow, blue in slots 1, 2, 4; now those same three colors sit as yellow, blue, white. Checking against the first cut confirms it's the same operation: colors of remaining whole wires rotate one slot left after each correct cut, cut stubs stay put. And the light stepped again: yellow → green → now white. Display still 0. That's a predictable bomb, which is worth more than it sounds — Mute can now anticipate the post-cut state instead of waiting on me, and I can verify Mute's expectations against what I actually see. Mute's 👍 I read as receipt of Blind's spoken after-action report, 👋 as "your board, Deaf" — so as promised, here is the full fresh report, plus the pattern, plus the standing protocol: ✊+number for another cut, ✋ if the next action isn't a cut, 👌 if the bomb is safe.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, full fresh report as promised. The system confirms the second cut was correct. Changes: the light has gone from green to WHITE, display still reads zero, and wire five is now cut. Current board, left to right: one yellow, two blue, three cut stub, four white, five cut stub. Two stubs now, at positions three and five; three whole wires at one, two, four. Also, I cracked the pattern. After each correct cut, the colors of the remaining whole wires rotate one position left among the whole-wire slots, wrapping around, and the stubs never move. Check it against the first cut: whole wires were green, white, yellow, blue, and after they read white, yellow, blue, green. It held again this time. The light also steps color each cut: yellow, then green, now white. So after any next cut you can predict my board before I report it, and I will verify. My questions: does the manual reference the white light? Does it give more cuts? If yes, sign ✊ and the number as before. If the next action is not a cut, sign ✋ first and we will build its meaning together. If that was the last step and the bomb is safe, sign 👌. Blind gave you the spoken report of the cut, I take your first 👍 as that being clean — sign ✋ if anything in it was wrong.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Your second cut was correct — system confirmed, and Mute heard your report. Well done. What I see now: the light is WHITE, display still zero, and both your cuts show: the middle stub at position three and the fifth position are both cut. By feel you should find two cut stubs — middle and one end — and three whole wires. Warning, same as before: the colors on the whole wires have rotated again, so trust positions only by recounting: display up, counting from your left, whole wires sit at one, two, and four, stubs at three and five. Hold still and touch nothing until the next rule arrives from me by voice. Keep speaking to Mute anything you sense — clicks, hums, warmth, any change in the bomb's body. Mute will send the next instruction and I will relay it with the word confirmed only after every check passes, same as last time.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ☝ 👍]

Third instruction decoded: ✊☝ — "cut, one." Wire 1, the yellow end wire, outermost left. The double 👍👍 answers my questions — yes on the white light, yes more cuts — and 🫵☝👍 mirrors turn 5's authorization pattern: "you — one — yes." Same dance as before, and wire 1 is an end wire, so the left-right trap applies again — but this time I have a stronger tactile check than last round: the *other* end is a stub. Blind can feel that position five is already cut, so if Blind finds a whole wire at the left end and a stub at the right end, the frame is proven before any blade moves. I've also extended the rotation law, so I can hand Mute a prediction to check against the manual before the cut — if the manual disagrees with my law, that's a ✋ moment. Protocol as established: plan-back by voice, relay as 👍/👎, my "confirmed" releases the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoding: ✊☝ is cut, wire one. The double thumbs-up answers my questions — yes on the white light, yes more cuts — and 🫵☝👍 I read as you, one, yes, proceed as before. So: same safety dance as the fifth wire. Blind will speak a plan-back to you. Relay it to me as 👍 if it matches these words exactly: display up, counting from my left, the wire I will cut is the first, the end wire on my left — or 👎 with finger counts for what differs. Before that, check my prediction against the manual. My rotation law says: after this cut, stubs sit at one, three, and five, whole wires at two and four, and the colors rotate — wire two should read white and wire four blue after the cut. Light I cannot predict, display should stay zero. If the manual says anything different about what follows this cut, sign ✋ before Blind touches anything. Once your 👍 on the plan-back reaches me, I will say the word confirmed and Blind cuts wire one. If this cut is the last step, sign 👌 after it; if more follow, ✊ and the number; if not a cut, ✋ first.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Next instruction from Mute: cut wire ONE this time — the outermost wire at the very LEFT end. End wire again, so same frame as before: display panel up, counting from your left. Here is your tactile proof before you commit. At position five, the far RIGHT end, you must feel a cut stub — you cut it yourself last time. At the LEFT end you must feel a whole wire. Between that left end wire and the middle stub there should be exactly one whole wire, so from the left: whole wire, whole wire, stub, whole wire, stub. If you feel a stub at the left end or a whole wire at the right end, the frame has slipped — touch nothing and say so. If the layout matches, speak aloud to Mute, word for word: display up, counting from my left, the wire I will cut is the first, the end wire on my left. Then wait. My voice saying the word confirmed is the only release, same as last time. One cut, one wire, then hands off and report everything you sense to Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ☝ 👍]

No ✋ in the batch, and the shape is familiar from turn 5: [👍👍] answers my two checks — Blind's plan-back matched word for word, and my rotation prediction (after this cut: wire two white, wire four blue, stubs at one, three, five) squared with the manual. [🫵☝👍] is the same go-signature as before: you — one — yes. Every gate I demanded has opened: frame proven by stub-at-the-other-end, plan-back verified, manual consistent with my law of the board. This is the moment to release the blade, with the geometry restated one final time so nothing drifts at the moment of truth. I'll also set up the after-cut verification: I predict a specific board, Mute's manual should agree, and if what I see next round disagrees with either, everything stops.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Everything checked: your plan-back matched word for word, Mute confirmed the manual agrees, and this is the authorization. The word is: confirmed. Cut now. Restating the target so nothing drifts. Display panel at the top, counting from your left. From the left you must feel: whole wire, whole wire, stub, whole wire, stub. The FIRST wire — the outermost one at the very LEFT end, with nothing beyond it and exactly one whole wire between it and the middle stub — that is the cut. One cut, one wire, nothing else. The instant it is done: hands off completely, and speak aloud to Mute everything you perceive — any click or snap, whether the wire falls slack, any hum, any warmth, anything at all. Then wait for my voice before touching the bomb again.")
```
